mainTopic: Using a non-Jew and ביטול רשות to bring water for a מילה on שבת, and the שיתוף in רבה and אביי's alleyway, including בְּרֵירָה with stored food
overview: This amud opens by finishing an objection to רבה, who let a non-Jew carry hot water for a baby's מילה on שבת. Telling a non-Jew is only a שבות, and so is הזאה, which does not override שבת. The answer is that a שבות involving an action is stricter, and רבה only had the non-Jew carry the water, not heat it. רבה בר רב חנן then asks אביי why their alleyway has no עירוב or שיתוף. אביי explains why no one arranges it, and why he cannot make the שיתוף with his own bread or with an unmarked רביעית of vinegar in a barrel. Two ברייתות disagree about using stored food for a שיתוף. רב אושעיא explains that they follow בית שמאי and בית הלל, who argue about בְּרֵירָה, as a משנה about a corpse in a house with many doorways shows. The amud then tells two stories of a baby whose warm water for the מילה spilled. In the first, רבא allows a גוי to heat water for the mother. In the second, רבא gives up his rights in his courtyard, relying on רבי יוחנן against שמואל. רבינא's follow-up question begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Telling a non-Jew is like sprinkling: neither overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: The objection concludes with a comparison: just as הזאה is a שבות that does not override שבת, so is אמירה לעכו"ם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as sprinkling is only a rabbinic prohibition and still does not override שבת, so too telling a non-Jew to do work is only a rabbinic prohibition and does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes an objection against רבה, who let a non-Jew bring hot water for a baby's מילה on שבת. The objector says that asking a non-Jew is a שבות, and a שבות does not get pushed aside even for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model case is הזאה. Sprinkling purifying water is only rabbinically forbidden on שבת, yet we do not permit it even so that someone can bring a קרבן פסח. The objector applies the same rule to אמירה לעכו"ם: it is also just a שבות, so it should not be allowed even for מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of the purifying water (מי חטאת) on someone who is טמא מת
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת, not a Torah-level מלאכה
Overrides (pushes aside) the laws of שבת
Telling a non-Jew to do a forbidden act on שבת

phrases.english: Just as sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition,
and it does not override Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Even for the sake of the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: so too telling a non-Jew is a rabbinic prohibition,
and it does not override Shabbat.
phrases.notes: So how could רבה allow it for the מילה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הַזָּאָה שְׁבוּת, וְאֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes an objection that began on the previous amud, against רבה's ruling to use a non-Jew for the מילה water.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's permission to have a non-Jew bring hot water on שבת for a מילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A הקש from הזאה: a שבות does not override שבת even for a מצוה. אמירה לעכו"ם is also a שבות, so it should not be permitted for מילה either.

steps.title: A rabbinic prohibition with an action differs from one without an action
steps.stepSummary: The defense distinguishes a שבות that involves a physical action, like הזאה, from one that does not. רבה never told the non-Jew to heat water, only to carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't you see the difference between a rabbinic prohibition that involves an action and one that doesn't? After all, the Master did not tell the non-Jew, 'Go heat the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer, which some attribute to רב יוסף, defends רבה by showing that the comparison to הזאה does not work. רבה's case was a lighter kind of שבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הזאה is a שבות in which the Jew himself performs an act, so it is stricter. Telling a non-Jew to carry something through a חצר without an עירוב involves no act by the Jew, and it is only a minor rabbinic issue. רבה deliberately avoided the stricter request of asking the non-Jew to heat water (בישול), which would be a Torah-level מלאכה done for a Jew.
steps.confusionAlert: "מר" here refers to רבה in the third person. The speaker is defending רבה, not describing himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a lasting principle: not every שבות is equal. A שבות without an action can be relaxed for a מצוה where a שבות with an action cannot.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you not differentiate
between a rabbinic prohibition that involves an action
and a rabbinic prohibition that does not involve an action?
For the Master did not say to the non-Jew:
Go heat (water).
phrases.notes: He only had him carry already-hot water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא שָׁנֵי לָךְ בֵּין שְׁבוּת דְּאִית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה לִשְׁבוּת דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by rejecting the comparison to הזאה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between two types of שבות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All rabbinic prohibitions are equal, so none overrides שבת for a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שבות without an action, like having a non-Jew carry, may be permitted for מילה. A שבות with an action, like הזאה, may not.

steps.title: How can an alleyway with two great scholars lack an עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן asks אביי how an alleyway housing רבה and אביי could have neither an עירוב nor a שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן said to אביי: An alleyway that has two great men, Torah scholars, living in it, and it has neither an עירוב nor a שיתוף?!
steps.whatsHappening: The whole problem only arose because there was no עירוב in the alleyway. So רבה בר רב חנן challenges אביי about how this could happen where great חכמים live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is rhetorical and works as a rebuke. תלמידי חכמים should make sure the basic עירובין of their neighborhood are in place. A שיתוף מבואות would have allowed carrying in the alleyway, and then there would have been no need for a non-Jew at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: עירוב חצרות, joining the houses of a courtyard
שיתוף מבואות, merging courtyards to permit carrying in the alleyway

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Chanan said to Abaye:
An alleyway that has in it
two great men such as the Sages,
phrases.notes: רבה and אביי.

phrases.aramaic: לָא לֶיהֱוֵי בֵּיהּ לָא עֵירוּב וְלֹא שִׁיתּוּף?!
phrases.english: should there be neither an eruv nor a shituf in it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבוֹאָה דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תְּרֵי גַּבְרֵי רַבְרְבֵי כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic defense to questioning the situation that caused the problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The absence of an עירוב and שיתוף in רבה and אביי's alleyway
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great scholars should be the first to ensure carrying is permitted. Their failure to do so is surprising.

steps.title: אביי explains why no one arranged the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that each person in the alleyway has a reason for not arranging it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What can we do? The Master (רבה), it is not his way. Me, I am busy with my learning. Them (the other residents), they don't pay attention.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by going through each party in the alleyway and saying why that party does not set up the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is too distinguished to go around collecting food from every resident. אביי is absorbed in his learning. The other residents simply do not care about such matters. So no one ends up doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not his way / not befitting him

phrases.english: He said to him: What should we do?
The Master, it is not his manner.
phrases.notes: To collect from the neighbors.

phrases.english: I am busy with my studies.
They do not attend to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה בר רב חנן's challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each party had a reason, so it was left undone.

steps.title: Why אביי cannot donate his own bread for the שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: אביי heads off the suggestion that he give his own bread to everyone. Since he could not actually hand it over if they asked, the שיתוף would be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if I were to transfer to them a share of the bread in my basket, since if they wanted it from me I could not give it to them, the שיתוף would be void.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers an unspoken follow-up: why not make the שיתוף yourself by giving the residents a share in your bread? He explains that it would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיתוף requires the residents to truly own a share of the food. אביי was poor and needed his bread. If they came to take it, he would not give it. So their ownership would not be real, and the שיתוף would be בטל.
steps.whatToRemember: A שיתוף works only if the residents genuinely own a share of the food. If the donor would not actually let them take it, the שיתוף is invalid.

phrases.english: And if I would transfer to them bread in my basket —
since if they wanted it from me
and it would be impossible for me to give it to them,
phrases.notes: Because אביי was poor and needed it.

phrases.english: the merging would be void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends אביי's answer by ruling out the obvious alternative solution.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי could make the שיתוף alone by giving everyone a share of his bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without a real willingness to hand the bread over, the שיתוף is invalid.

steps.title: A ברייתא: if a resident is refused food, the merging is void
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי's claim. If a resident asks for wine or oil from the שיתוף and is refused, the שיתוף is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: If one of the residents of an alleyway asked for wine or oil from the שיתוף and they did not give it to him, the שיתוף is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up what אביי just said in Step 5. It quotes a ברייתא showing that a שיתוף you cannot actually take from is not a real שיתוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיתוף works because every resident is a true partner in the food. If someone asks for his share and is turned away, it becomes clear that he was never really a partner, so the שיתוף collapses. This is exactly why אביי says his own bread would not work: he could not really hand it over if the others asked.

keyTerms.meaning: Merging of the alleyway: shared food that allows carrying in the alleyway on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a שיתוף depends on real partnership, not just a formal gesture. The food must truly be available to every partner.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One of the residents of an alleyway
who asked for wine or oil (from the shared food),
and they did not give it to him —
the merging (shituf) is void.
phrases.notes: It turns out he was never a real partner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for אביי's claim in Step 5 that a שיתוף he could not actually hand over would be invalid.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that giving bread he could not truly hand over would make the שיתוף invalid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a resident who requests wine or oil and is refused voids the שיתוף.

steps.title: Why not set aside a little vinegar from a barrel?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן suggests that אביי give the residents a רביעית of vinegar from one of his barrels. That small amount would surely be easy to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the Master transfer to them a רביעית of vinegar in a barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנן pushes back on אביי again. He suggests a tiny amount of vinegar that אביי could easily afford to give if asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in Step 5 was that אביי could not really give away bread if the residents demanded it. A רביעית of vinegar is so small that אביי could clearly give it, so the problem seems to disappear. The question is: why not set up the שיתוף this way?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him transfer ownership (give them a share)
A רביעית, a quarter-לוג (a small measure)

phrases.english: But let the Master transfer to them
a quarter-log of vinegar in a barrel.
phrases.notes: A cheap, tiny amount that he could surely give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to get around the problem from Steps 5–6 by proposing an amount so small that אביי could certainly give it.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that he cannot make the שיתוף himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only problem is not being able to hand the food over, a tiny amount of vinegar solves it. So אביי has no excuse.

steps.title: Food in a storeroom cannot be used for a merging
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a ברייתא: one may not make a שיתוף with food in an אוצר. A רביעית that is not marked off inside a barrel is the same kind of case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: One may not make a שיתוף with food in a storeroom.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a ברייתא. Food mixed into a larger stockpile cannot be used for a שיתוף, and a רביעית inside a full barrel is like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an אוצר, it is not clear which specific portion belongs to the שיתוף. The same is true of a רביעית of vinegar inside a whole barrel, since no particular vinegar has been set aside. So the vinegar idea fails, not because of cost but because the portion is not defined.

keyTerms.meaning: A storeroom or stockpile of food

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is NOT that the vinegar is too little or too expensive. The problem is that the share is not clearly identified inside the barrel.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
One may not make a merging with food in a storeroom.
phrases.notes: It is unclear which specific portion is set aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the vinegar suggestion in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source with a rule that disqualifies the proposed method.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tiny amount of vinegar from a barrel should work, since אביי could easily give it.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unmarked portion inside a larger stock, like an אוצר, cannot serve as a שיתוף.

steps.title: But another ברייתא allows a storeroom
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן points to a different ברייתא that says one may make a שיתוף with food in an אוצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: One may make a שיתוף with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's source. Another ברייתא says the exact opposite: an אוצר may be used for a שיתוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two ברייתות that contradict each other. If the ברייתא that permits an אוצר is correct, the vinegar suggestion from Step 7 would work again.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught? (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: One may make a merging (with stored food)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא אביי quoted in Step 8 by citing a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that forbids using an אוצר for a שיתוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות contradict each other. If one permits it, אביי cannot rely on the one that forbids it.

steps.title: One ברייתא follows בית שמאי, the other בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא resolves the contradiction. The ברייתא that forbids follows בית שמאי, and the ברייתא that permits follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: It is not difficult. This one follows בית שמאי, and that one follows בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא settles the clash between the two ברייתות. They reflect two different opinions: בית שמאי forbid using an אוצר, and בית הלל allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The underlying question is whether we can say that the portion chosen later was the one meant all along (ברירה, retroactive clarification). בית הלל accept this idea, so stored food works. בית שמאי do not, so stored food fails.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the contradiction can be resolved)
Retroactive clarification: what is chosen later is treated as having been chosen from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Usually we follow בית הלל, so this answer seems to make the vinegar idea valid again. The rest of this amud never returns to that question. After proving the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute (Steps 11–13), the גמרא moves on to a new story about spilled water. So do not expect the vinegar issue to be settled here.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
It is not difficult;
this one (forbidding) follows Beit Shammai,
that one (permitting) follows Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes each source to a different תנאים opinion (בית שמאי vs. בית הלל).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות are a true contradiction about the same law.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a dispute: בית שמאי forbid using an אוצר and בית הלל permit it, based on whether ברירה applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It links the practical question of the שיתוף to a basic principle, ברירה, which comes up all over the תלמוד.

steps.title: The source: a corpse in a house with many doorways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה to show where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree. When a corpse is in a house with many doorways, all the doorways are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If a corpse is in a house, and the house has many doorways, they are all impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof for רב אושעיא's claim by starting to quote a משנה. This first line gives the basic case, and the משנה continues next to the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which doorway will be used to carry the corpse out. So every doorway is treated as impure, as if the corpse already passed through it. Like the vinegar in the barrel, this is a case of not knowing which part will later be chosen, which is why it is the right place to see the dispute over ברירה.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If a corpse is in a house,
and it has many doorways —
they are all impure.
phrases.notes: Any doorway might be the one used to take the corpse out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source that grounds רב אושעיא's claim that בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about this kind of case.
steps.raayaObject: רב אושעיא's claim that the two ברייתות reflect a בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a corpse in a house with many doorways. The dispute itself appears in the continuation of the משנה later.

steps.title: Choosing one exit saves the other doorways
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If only one doorway is open, only that one is impure. If someone decides to take the body out through one doorway, or through a window of four by four טפחים, all the other doorways stay pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only one of the doorways was open, that one is impure and all the others are pure. If a person decided to take the body out through one of the doorways, or through a window that is four by four טפחים, that decision saves all the other doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה it started in step 11. It is laying the groundwork for the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the doorways are impure only because we don't know which one the body will leave through. Once that is known, whether because only one door is open or because a person decides, only that exit is impure. The question about to come up is when such a decision has to be made for it to count.

keyTerms.meaning: He decided, he made up his mind

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the corpse has to be moved for the decision to work. Simply deciding on the exit is enough to save the other doorways.

phrases.english: If one of them was open,
phrases.notes: Only one doorway is actually open.

phrases.english: that one is impure, and all the others are pure.
phrases.notes: The body will clearly leave through the open door.

phrases.english: If he decided to take it out through one of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בַּחַלּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: or through a window that is four by four (טפחים),
phrases.notes: A window this size is large enough to count as an exit.

phrases.english: it saves all the doorways.
phrases.notes: Every doorway other than the chosen one stays pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְתַּח אֶחָד מֵהֶן הוּא טָמֵא וְכוּלָּן טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה begun in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב אושעיא's claim that the two ברייתות about a שיתוף with stored food reflect the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a corpse in a house with many doorways (אהלות)

steps.title: When the decision must be made: before or after death
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say the decision about the exit counts only if it was made before the person died. בית הלל say it counts even if it was made after the death.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: this works only if he decided before the person died. בית הלל say: it works even if he decided after the person died.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the dispute the גמרא was looking for. It finishes the proof for רב אושעיא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity spreads at the moment of death. If the decision comes later, it can only work by revealing, after the fact, which exit was 'chosen' all along. This is retroactive choice, called בְּרֵירָה. בית הלל accept it, so an unmarked רביעית inside a barrel can count for a שיתוף, while בית שמאי reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive choice: a later decision shows what was 'chosen' from the start

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל accept retroactive choice (בְּרֵירָה) and בית שמאי do not. That is why a שיתוף from unmarked stored food is allowed according to בית הלל and forbidden according to בית שמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a law about corpse impurity to the laws of שיתוף. Both depend on one principle: whether a decision made later can define something after the fact.

phrases.english: בית שמאי say:

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁחִישֵּׁב עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָמוּת הַמֵּת.
phrases.english: This applies only if he decided before the person died.
phrases.notes: No retroactive choice is allowed.

phrases.english: And בית הלל say:
Even after the person has died.
phrases.notes: Retroactive choice (בְּרֵירָה) works.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים וְהוּא שֶׁחִישֵּׁב עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָמוּת הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה and gives the dispute that proves רב אושעיא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב אושעיא's answer that the forbidding ברייתא follows בית שמאי and the permitting ברייתא follows בית הלל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute in the משנה over whether a decision made after death works (בְּרֵירָה)

steps.title: רבא's ruling: heat water through the mother
steps.stepSummary: A baby's warm water for his מילה spilled on שבת. רבא says to ask the mother. If she needs warm water, a גוי may heat it for her, and the baby can use it as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain baby whose warm water spilled. רבא said to them: Let us ask his mother. If she needs it, a גוי may heat water for him by way of his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story with a ruling from רבא about a problem on שבת. It is a separate case from the שיתוף discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating water just for the מילה would not be allowed on שבת. A woman who just gave birth (יוֹלֶדֶת) is treated as possibly in danger, so water may be heated for her. Once it is heated for her, the baby may use it too.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who just gave birth

steps.confusionAlert: The heating is permitted for the mother's health, not for the מילה. The baby only benefits from water that was heated for her.

phrases.english: There was a certain baby whose warm water spilled,
phrases.notes: The water had been prepared for his מילה on שבת.

phrases.english: רבא said to them:
Let us ask his mother.
If she needs it,
let a גוי heat it for him by way of his mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with a separate ruling, not part of the בְּרֵירָה proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the mother needs warm water, a גוי may heat it for her, and the baby may use it for his מילה.

steps.title: The mother is eating dates, so she seems healthy
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא objects that the mother is eating dates. That suggests she is not in danger, so heating water for her should not be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to רבא: His mother is eating dates!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא challenges רבא's ruling. He points out that the mother appears healthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling depends on the mother being in possible danger. If she is well enough to eat dates, the reason for permitting the heating seems to fall away.

phrases.english: רב משרשיא said to רבא:
His mother is eating dates!
phrases.notes: This implies she is healthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְרָבָא אִימֵּיהּ קָא אָכְלָה תַּמְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's assumption that the mother may need heated water for her health
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone eating dates seems healthy, so there is no danger that would permit heating water for her.

steps.title: It may just be a ravenous hunger
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that her eating may be only a sudden ravenous hunger. It does not prove she is healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I can say that it is just a ravenous hunger that has seized her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. He explains that her eating does not show she is well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sudden, overwhelming hunger can grip a sick person. So eating dates says nothing about her real condition. She may still be in danger, and the permission stands.

keyTerms.meaning: I can say, it is possible that

steps.whatToRemember: A woman who just gave birth keeps her status as possibly in danger even if she seems to eat normally. So a גוי may heat water for her on שבת, and her baby may benefit from it.

phrases.english: He (רבא) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר, תּוּנְבָּא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּנָקֵט לַהּ.
phrases.english: I can say it is just a ravenous hunger that has seized her.
phrases.notes: Her eating does not prove she is healthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר תּוּנְבָּא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּנָקֵט לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב משרשיא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating dates shows the mother is healthy and does not need heated water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her eating may come from a sudden ravenous hunger, so she may still be in danger, and heating water for her is allowed.

steps.title: רבא's plan to bring warm water to the baby
steps.stepSummary: A baby's warm water for his מילה spilled. רבא tells his household to move his belongings from the men's room to the women's room. He will sit there and give up his rights in his courtyard to the people of the baby's courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain baby whose warm water spilled. רבא said to them: Clear my things out of the men's room and into the women's room. I will go and sit there, and I will give up my rights in this courtyard to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. רבא gives practical instructions so the warm water in his courtyard can reach the baby on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two courtyards had no עירוב between them, so nobody could carry the water from one to the other. רבא's fix is ביטול רשות: he gives up his rights in his courtyard so that it counts as belonging to the baby's side. He moves his things to the inner women's room, which does not open straight into the courtyard, so he will not forget and carry them into a courtyard he no longer has rights in.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby (here, one about to have his ברית מילה)
His warm water (heated for the מילה)
The men's room, which opens directly into the courtyard
The women's room, an inner room that does not open into the courtyard
I will give up (my rights). This is the act of ביטול רשות.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not move his belongings to make room. He moves them because once he gives up his rights in the courtyard, he may no longer carry from his own room into it. Keeping his things in the inner room protects him from forgetting and carrying them out.

phrases.english: A certain baby whose warm water spilled,
phrases.notes: The water was for washing the baby at his מילה on שבת.

phrases.english: Rava said to them:
Clear away my belongings
from the men's room to the women's room,
phrases.notes: Out of the room that opens into the courtyard and into the inner room.

phrases.english: and I will go and sit there
and I will give up to them my rights in this courtyard.
phrases.notes: He gives up his rights to the people of the baby's courtyard so the water can be carried across.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with a case similar to Step 14 (spilled water for a baby's מילה). This time the solution is ביטול רשות rather than heating water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there is no עירוב, a person may give up his rights in his courtyard to the residents of a neighboring courtyard so they can carry the warm water needed for a מילה.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל: giving up rights does not work between courtyards
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבא. שמואל said that ביטול רשות does not work from one courtyard to a different courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: But didn't שמואל say that there is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another courtyard?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רבא's plan, using a ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול רשות normally works between people who share the same courtyard. שמואל holds that it cannot pass from one courtyard to a separate one. רבא's plan depends on exactly that kind of transfer, so by שמואל's rule it should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (so-and-so) say? This phrase introduces a challenge from an established ruling.
Giving up one's rights in a shared area so others may carry there
From one courtyard to another, separate courtyard

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava,
But didn't Shmuel say:
There is no renouncing of rights from courtyard to courtyard?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method רבא proposed in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's plan to give up his rights in his courtyard to the residents of a different courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that ביטול רשות does not work from one courtyard to another, so רבא's ביטול should have no effect.

steps.title: רבא follows רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he follows רבי יוחנן, who holds that ביטול רשות does work from one courtyard to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: I hold like רבי יוחנן, who said: there is giving up of rights from one courtyard to another.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his plan. He relies on a different אמורא who disagrees with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not argue that שמואל's rule fits this case. He simply rules against שמואל and follows רבי יוחנן, who allows ביטול between courtyards. Under that view, his plan works.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת: שמואל says ביטול רשות does not work between two courtyards, and רבי יוחנן says it does. רבא follows רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I hold in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: There is renouncing from courtyard to courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the opposing authority (רבי יוחנן) instead of שמואל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ביטול should fail because of שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows רבי יוחנן, so ביטול between courtyards works and his plan stands.

steps.title: רבינא begins a follow-up challenge
steps.stepSummary: רבינא starts a new question: if רבא does not follow שמואל, then... The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the Master does not hold like שמואל...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רבינא is opening a follow-up challenge, and the full question comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא accepts that רבא rejects שמואל. He is about to ask about a consequence of that choice, probably suggesting that רבא's plan could have been even simpler. The actual point of the challenge has not been stated yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (a respectful way to say 'you')
And if he does not hold it (that view)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: But if the Master does not hold in accordance with Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The sentence is unfinished here. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's answer in Step 19 to set up a further challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's practical procedure, given that he rejects שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. It draws a consequence from רבא rejecting שמואל, and the full argument continues on the next amud.
